spike.c: NOT stated in Vercel's docs; confirmed from the CLI's source and from CLI-written files, not by running the CLI. Docs read (cli/env, cli/pull, environment-variables, system-environment-variables, deployments/environments), paraphrased: env pull exports the project's variables to a file (.env.local by default, also with --environment), and VERCEL_ENV is a system variable present at build and run time, valued production, preview or development; no page says whether env pull writes system variables. CLI source (vercel/vercel packages/cli/src/commands/env/pull.ts): it writes every record the env-pull API returns (pullEnvRecords(client, pullId, source, { target: environment || 'development', gitBranch })), dropping only VERCEL_ANALYTICS_ID, VERCEL_SPEED_INSIGHTS_ID and VERCEL_WEB_ANALYTICS_ID, under the header '# Created by Vercel CLI'. Public files carrying that header (GitHub code search) hold VERCEL_ENV="development" (default pulls) and VERCEL_ENV="production" (production pulls, e.g. several '.env.vercel.prod' files — a custom file name, which only 'vercel env pull <file>' writes, since 'vercel pull' uses fixed paths under .vercel/) — so yes, a production pull writes VERCEL_ENV="production" when the project exposes system variables, which this plan requires to be on (Choice 12, Task 17). Found on the way, and it widens S1: Secret variables are written as a placeholder (the env docs say so when the local file has no real value for the key); source: SENSITIVE_ENV_VALUE_PLACEHOLDER = '[SENSITIVE]' (packages/cli/src/util/env/constants.ts), assigned for every Secret key with no local value, file present or not. A production pull therefore also writes SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN="[SENSITIVE]", which next.config.ts would take as a token. The vercel CLI was not run.
spike.d: This worktree: no web/.env* and no root .env* file; no .vercel folder; the only tracked env file is server/.env.example. The root .gitignore covers them at any depth: lines 21-25 '.env', '.env.*', '*.env', 'jira.env', '!.env.example'. Outside this worktree, names only: the primary checkout has web/.env — 0 bytes, git-ignored by '.gitignore:23:*.env', not opened — and no .vercel folder; no other worktree's web/ has a .env* file.
spike.e: Compatible. The Task 2 Step 5 script would read: "build": "node scripts/vendor-alphatab.mjs && NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION=$(node scripts/app-version.mjs) VERCEL_ENV=$VERCEL_ENV next build && node scripts/assert-design-system-css.mjs && node scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs". app-version.mjs (and assert-no-auth-token.mjs) run as their own node processes and never load .env files, so they already read only the shell's VERCEL_ENV; the pin makes next.config.ts read the same value, so the release name and the upload gate can no longer disagree (today, with VERCEL_ENV=production only in a .env file and a token in the shell, the upload would run under release 'local'). On Vercel, web/vercel.json's buildCommand is 'rm -rf .next/cache && pnpm run build', so the pin runs there too and passes Vercel's own value through unchanged; the e2e lane builds with 'pnpm build' (webServer), also covered. '' and unset behave the same downstream: Next 16.3.6 reads VERCEL_ENV only as === 'preview' (dist/lib/metadata/metadata.js:296, resolvers/resolve-url.js:66), and Sentry's getVercelEnv() is 'process.env.VERCEL_TARGET_ENV || process.env.VERCEL_ENV || undefined' (sentry-javascript develop; @sentry/nextjs is not installed here to check 11.1.0). The POSIX 'VAR=$VAR cmd' form adds no portability limit: the script already uses NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION=$(…) and pnpm runs it with sh. If adopted: Task 1 Step 4's comment should say the build script hands next build the shell's own VERCEL_ENV, and putting the pin in Task 1 keeps the gate and its guard in one commit (Task 2 also works). The pin does not cover 'pnpm dev' (scripts/dev.mjs spawns next dev, which also reads .env.local): dev never uploads, but before Task 17 adds the slugs the slug check would throw there. Alternative of equal strength: gate on the release the script computed (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION?.startsWith('v0.')) — always set on the command line, so a .env file cannot change it — but it ties the upload to the version format; the pin is simpler. Why it is not happening today: no web/.env* and no Vercel CLI link anywhere, and a default 'vercel env pull' writes VERCEL_ENV="development" (gate off). It needs a deliberate production pull into web/ (or a hand-written line). Then: with a token in the shell, a real upload into the production project (release 'local'); with no token in the shell, the '[SENSITIVE]' placeholder makes every local 'pnpm build' and the e2e lane's build fail — the slug check before Task 17, Sentry refusing the token after. The pin prevents both. Not covered by the pin: the same pull writes NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN's real value (NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are stored as Config, so they are readable), so 'pnpm dev' and local builds would report into the production project, against D5 — the e2e lane is safe, as its webServer env sets the fake DSN, which a .env file cannot override. One README or web/AGENTS.md line ('never pull Production variables into web/') would cover that too.
